# Tool-call compatibility matrix

Every cell states what is proven, for which client version, on which caller-to-upstream path, with the evidence that proves it. A combination that is not proven is listed as not covered with its reason, never omitted. Last matrix update: 2026-11-02.

A `mock` cell is a deterministic scripted upstream; a `unit` cell is a local conversion check with no endpoint call; a `live` cell ran against a real provider and carries its date, commit, cost and cost source. Mock and live evidence are never merged into one result. The underlying per-suite evidence lives in [bounded tool-call proof](tool-call-proof) and [live API compatibility](api-compatibility-live).

## Rerun

Mock, unit and path cells:

```sh
make agent-tool-mock    # pinned clients against a scripted upstream
make agent-chain-mock   # depth matrix, writes tests/agent_compat/.out/chain-matrix.json
make compat-mock        # pinned OpenAI and Anthropic SDK suites
python3 scripts/tool_compat_matrix.py --check
```

Live rows are recorded runs, not a schedule: every one names its date and commit. Recurring nightlies need repository Actions secrets that do not exist yet (tracked in issue #572, `NEEDS CHETAN`); until they exist, a live cell is updated by an authorized manual run whose report is ingested with `--ingest`.

## Limits

- A mock cell proves a client and the router exchange the expected shapes against a scripted upstream; it does not prove live provider behaviour for the same request.
- A live row is one recorded run on the named commit, not a pass rate; the parallel gate is a two-turn HTTP probe, not a named client library run.
- Combinations and depth values that are not listed are untested, never passing.
- Provider-hosted tools are rejected before dispatch with 400 provider-hosted-tools-forbidden by contract; no cell claims them as supported.
- Costs come from the router's usage rows at configured list prices or from the provider's own bill; they are not invoices unless the row says so, and a run-scoped cost is not a per-cell attribution.
- opencode and aider have no cell; their fixtures verify a workload, not a real client tool loop.
- Nightly live automation is not enabled yet because the required Actions secrets do not exist (issue #572), so no cell is updated on a schedule.
